hook: Salt is hard enough to grind teeth on, yet one tap with a spoon shatters a crystal. It survives a hot stove without melting, yet dry salt will not carry a current. All of these come from one picture: billions of ions packed in a pattern where every ion is surrounded by opposite charges.

prereq.q: Which pair of ions attracts more strongly, at the same distance apart?
prereq.why: Coulomb's law: the attraction grows with the product of the charges, 4 for Ca²⁺ and O²⁻ against 1 for the others.

options: a cation and an anion, usually from a metal and a nonmetal
two nonmetal atoms sharing a pair of electrons
metal cations and a sea of electrons
prereq.why: The metal gives up electrons and the nonmetal takes them; the ions attract.

figure.caption: Left: in an ionic solid every ion is surrounded by ions of the opposite charge. Right: a force that shifts one layer brings like charges side by side; they repel, and the crystal splits.

chain.cause: Cations and anions attract every nearby ion of opposite charge
chain.effect: they settle in a repeating three-dimensional lattice, each ion surrounded by opposite charges

chain.cause: Every ion is held by several strong Coulombic attractions
chain.effect: a lot of energy is needed to free the ions, so the melting temperature is high

chain.cause: Larger charges and smaller ions give stronger attractions
chain.effect: the lattice energy and melting temperature are larger (MgO far above NaCl)

chain.cause: A force shifts one layer of ions
chain.effect: like charges line up and repel, so the solid is brittle

chain.cause: The ions are fixed in the solid but free to move when melted or dissolved
chain.effect: the solid does not conduct, but the melt and the solution do

ideas: An ionic solid is a repeating 3-D array of cations and anions; each ion is surrounded by opposite charges. There are no separate molecules.
Lattice energy grows with ion charge and shrinks with distance (Coulomb's law). Compare charges first, then sizes, for both compounds.
Strong attractions throughout the lattice give high melting temperatures and hardness.
Ionic solids are brittle: a shifted layer puts like charges side by side.
Ions carry the current: solid, no electrical conductivity; melted or dissolved, good conductivity.

misconception.wrong: Solid sodium chloride is made of NaCl molecules, each one Na⁺ stuck to one Cl⁻.
misconception.right: Each Na⁺ is surrounded by six Cl⁻ ions and attracted to all of them equally, and each Cl⁻ by six Na⁺. The formula NaCl gives the 1 : 1 ratio of ions in the lattice, not a molecule.

summary: An ionic solid is a lattice of alternating cations and anions in which every ion is attracted to its oppositely charged neighbors. Coulomb's law sets the lattice energy: larger charges and shorter distances between ion centers give stronger attraction and higher melting temperatures. Ionic solids are hard but brittle, because shifting a layer brings like charges together. They do not conduct as solids, but conduct when melted or dissolved because the ions can then move.
